title: Highest-Protein Nuts: Ranking per 100 Grams and per Ounce

seo.title: Highest-Protein Nuts per Serving
seo.meta_description: Compare almonds, pistachios, cashews, walnuts and hazelnuts by protein per 100 grams and per 1-ounce serving, plus peanuts for context.
seo.search_intent: Compare nuts by protein concentration and realistic serving.

excerpt: Almonds and pistachios lead the tree-nut ranking, but the number that matters in your hand is smaller: a 1-ounce serving gives roughly 6 grams of protein, not the 20-plus grams suggested by a 100-gram table.
content_html:
Nuts are a perfect example of how a 100-gram ranking can sound more dramatic than a normal serving. Almonds and pistachios top 20 grams of protein per 100 grams, but most people eat about 1 ounce / 28 grams at a time.

That does not make them poor protein foods. It simply defines their role: nuts are excellent at adding protein, fiber and unsaturated fat, but they are not especially lean protein sources.

From the 100-gram ranking to a handful

NutProtein/100 gProtein/1 oz
Almonds21.2 g5.9 g
Pistachios20.2 g5.7 g
Cashews18.2 g5.1 g
Walnuts15.2 g4.3 g
Hazelnuts15.0 g4.2 g
Brazil nuts14.3 g4.0 g
Pecans9.2 g2.6 g
Macadamias7.9 g2.2 g

Almonds and pistachios are basically tied by serving

Almonds contain about 21.2 g protein/100 g and pistachios 20.2 g. In a 1-ounce serving that becomes about 5.9 versus 5.7 g — a difference too small to matter in a normal snack.

Almonds also provide roughly 12.5 g fiber/100 g and substantial vitamin E; pistachios provide around 10 g fiber and are notable for vitamin B6 and potassium.

Cashews are closer than the ranking makes them look

Cashews provide about 18.2 g protein/100 g, or just over 5 g per ounce. Compared with the 5.9 g in almonds, the real-world gap is less than a gram.

Walnuts and hazelnuts bring different strengths

Both are around 15 g protein/100 g and about 4 g per ounce. Walnuts stand out for alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), a plant omega-3, while hazelnuts are rich in vitamin E and monounsaturated fat.

Pecans and macadamias sit much lower on protein

Pecans and macadamias are around 9.2 and 7.9 g/100 g. One ounce of macadamias provides about 2.2 g protein compared with nearly 6 g from almonds.

Peanuts would win — but they are legumes

Peanuts provide about 25.8 g protein/100 g and roughly 7.2 g per ounce. They are used like nuts in the kitchen, but botanically they belong to the legume family.

They are useful context, but putting them into a tree-nut ranking without explanation mixes two different categories.

Protein comes with a lot of energy here

Nuts generally contain 550 to more than 700 calories/100 g. Almonds are around 579 calories with 21.2 g protein, while cooked chicken breast is around 165 calories with 31 g protein.

Getting 30 g protein from almonds would take about 5 ounces / 142 g and more than 800 calories; chicken would require roughly 3.4 ounces / 97 g and about 160 calories. That does not make almonds a worse food. It shows that their nutritional job includes unsaturated fat, fiber and micronutrients, not just protein.

Raw or roasted? Additions usually matter more

Roasting changes moisture slightly. Salt, sugar, honey, chocolate or added oils usually change the final nutrition profile far more than roasting itself.

The useful takeaway

Almonds and pistachios are the highest-protein common tree nuts, but a normal ounce provides roughly 6 grams. Nuts are excellent supporting protein foods, not usually the most efficient centerpiece.

faq.question: Which nut has the most protein?
faq.answer: Among common tree nuts, almonds are about 21.2 g/100 g and pistachios 20.2 g/100 g.

faq.question: How much protein is in an ounce of nuts?
faq.answer: About 5.9 g in almonds, 5.7 g in pistachios, 5.1 g in cashews and 4.3 g in walnuts.

faq.question: Are peanuts higher in protein?
faq.answer: Yes, about 25.8 g/100 g, but peanuts are botanically legumes.
